faqs.q: How do I calculate my annual salary from an hourly rate under the national minimum wage australia?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours worked per week, then by 52. For a standard 38-hour week, annual gross = hourly × 38 × 52. For example, at the national minimum wage of $26.44, annual gross is $52,254.80.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the national minimum wage and award rates?

bodyMarkdown:
## Converting Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay: A Guide Using the National Minimum Wage Australia

If you're paid by the hour or considering a salary offer, understanding how your hourly rate translates to annual, fortnightly, and weekly pay is essential. This guide uses the **national minimum wage australia** as a starting point, but the same principles apply to any hourly rate. We'll walk through the calculation, explain the role of the Fair Work Commission, and cover tax, superannuation, and casual loading.

### The Basic Formula: Hourly × Hours per Week × 52

The standard method to estimate annual gross pay is:

**Annual gross = hourly rate × hours worked per week × 52 weeks**

This assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. For most full-time employees, the standard week is 38 hours, as defined by the Fair Work Ombudsman. When we refer to a full-time week, we assume 38 hours. If your hours differ, adjust accordingly.

For example, at the **national minimum wage australia** of $26.44 per hour (from 1 July 2026), working 38 hours per week:

- Weekly pay: $26.44 × 38 = $1,004.90
- Fortnightly pay: $1,004.90 × 2 = $2,009.80
- Annual gross: $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,254.80

This annual figure is before tax, the Medicare levy, and before superannuation (which is paid on top by your employer).

### Why the Fortnight Matters

Many Australian employers pay fortnightly. Knowing your fortnightly amount helps with budgeting and comparing salary offers. Simply double your weekly pay. For the **national minimum wage australia**, the fortnightly gross is $2,009.80. If you're a casual worker, remember that casual loading (see below) applies to each hour, so your fortnightly gross will be higher.

### National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates vs Enterprise Agreements

The **national minimum wage australia** is the legal minimum for employees not covered by an award or registered agreement. It is set annually by the Fair Work Commission. However, most industries have specific award rates that are higher. For example, the Hospitality Award or the General Retail Industry Award may set higher minimums for particular classifications.

If you are covered by an award, your employer must pay at least the award rate for your role. Some employers also have enterprise agreements that may offer different conditions. Always check your pay against the relevant award using the Fair Work Ombudsman's [pay guides](/blog) or [reference tables](/data). The **national minimum wage australia** is a floor, not a target for most workers.

### Casual Loading: What It Means for Your Pay

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on their base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave (annual, sick, personal) and other entitlements. The loading is added on top of the base rate. For the **national minimum wage australia**, the casual rate is $26.44 × 1.25 = $33.05 per hour.

When using our [timesheet](/), you can check a box to add 25% casual loading. Do not enter a rate that already includes casual loading – the tool adds it for you. Your annual gross as a casual at the **national minimum wage australia** would be $33.05 × 38 × 52 = $65,318.80 before tax and super.

### Superannuation: Paid on Top of Your Gross

Under the Superannuation Guarantee, your employer must pay superannuation contributions of 12% of your ordinary time earnings (as of 2026–27) into a super fund. This is on top of your gross pay, not deducted from it. The super guarantee applies up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per quarter (2026–27). For the **national minimum wage australia**, the annual super contribution would be 12% of $52,254.80 = $6,270.58, assuming you earn below the cap.

Super is not included in your take-home pay; it's additional retirement savings. When comparing a salary offer to an hourly rate, remember that super is paid on top of salary as well. For more details, see our guide on [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

### Estimating Tax and Take-Home Pay

Your annual gross is not what you take home. The Australian Taxation Office applies progressive tax rates for 2026–27:

- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% on excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: 30% on excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: 37% on excess over $135,000
- $190,001+: 45% on excess over $190,000

Plus, the Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. For the **national minimum wage australia** annual gross of $52,254.80, the tax estimate (using the 2026–27 scale and 2025–26 Medicare reduction thresholds) would be approximately:

- Tax on first $18,200: $0
- Tax on $18,201 to $45,000: ($45,000 - $18,200) × 15% = $4,020
- Tax on $45,001 to $52,254.80: ($52,254.80 - $45,000) × 30% = $2,176.44
- Total tax: $6,196.44
- Medicare levy (2% of $52,254.80): $1,045.10
- Total deductions: $7,241.54
- Estimated take-home: $45,013.26 annually, or about $865.64 per week.

Note: This is an estimate. It does not include HELP repayments, Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool for a more detailed calculation.

### What About Average Earnings?

The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports Average Weekly Earnings (AWE) for full-time adult ordinary time as $2,083.70 per week (May 2026). That's significantly higher than the **national minimum wage australia** weekly amount of $1,004.90. The AWE includes all full-time employees across industries and experience levels. It is an average, not a median, and not specific to any job. For job-specific pay, see our [job pay](/topics/job-pay) resources.

### When Hours Differ from 38

The formula works for any weekly hours. If you work 20 hours per week at the **national minimum wage australia**, annual gross = $26.44 × 20 × 52 = $27,497.60. For part-time or casual workers, your hours may vary each week; the annual estimate assumes consistent hours. Use our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool to explore different scenarios.

### Key Points to Remember

- The **national minimum wage australia** is $26.44 per hour for a 38-hour week (as at 1 July 2026).
- Casual loading of 25% applies on top of the base rate.
- Superannuation is 12% of ordinary earnings, paid by your employer on top.
- Tax and Medicare levy reduce your take-home pay.
- Award rates may be higher than the national minimum wage.
- Always check your specific circumstances with the Fair Work Ombudsman or a qualified advisor.

For a quick calculation, use our [timesheet](/). It allows you to enter your base hourly rate and add casual loading if applicable. The results show weekly, fortnightly, and annual gross, plus estimated tax and super.

Understanding your pay is the first step to financial planning. Whether you're on the **national minimum wage australia** or a higher rate, knowing how to convert hourly to annual helps you compare job offers, budget, and negotiate.
